_meta.active: BICTEGRAVIR SODIUM; EMTRICITABINE; TENOFOVIR ALAFENAMIDE FUMARATE
_meta.indication: Complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults with no antiretroviral treatment history or to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA less than 50 copies per mL) on a stable regimen for at least 3 months with no history of treatment failure and no known resistance substitutions

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (B/F/TAF vs ABC/DTG/3TC), 48 weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who achieved HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 as defined by the US FDA snapshot algorithm
pivotal_trials.result: HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48: 92.4% B/F/TAF vs 93% ABC/DTG/3TC; lower bound of 95.002% CI of difference -4.8% (> -12% NI margin), noninferiority demonstrated

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled (B/F/TAF vs DTG + F/TAF), 48 weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects who achieved HIV-1 RNA < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 as defined by the US FDA snapshot algorithm
pivotal_trials.result: HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48: 89.4% B/F/TAF vs 92.9% DTG/F/TAF; lower bound of 95.002% CI of difference -7.9% (> -12% NI margin), noninferiority demonstrated

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >= 5%, all grades) are diarrhea, nausea, and headache. In Trial 1489, diarrhea 6% (vs 4%), nausea 5% (vs 17%), headache 5% (vs 5%)
target_moa: Three-drug combination: bictegravir, an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) that blocks the integrase enzyme responsible for insertion of the viral genome into host cell DNA, plus emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide, two nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitors

boxed_warning.content: Post-treatment acute exacerbation of hepatitis B: severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in patients coinfected with HIV-1 and HBV who discontinued products containing emtricitabine and/or TDF, and may occur with discontinuation of BIKTARVY

rems.type: No identified safety issues warrant consideration of REMS

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not held for this NDA

description.text: Expanded patient population to include HIV-1 infected pediatric patients weighing at least 25 kg

citations.quote: - To expand the patient population for BIKTARVY® to include HIV-1 infected pediatric patients weighing at least 25 kg. This change is supported by safety and efficacy data in HIV-1 infected, virologically suppressed adolescents and children from Clinical Trial GS-US-380-1474.

description.text: Expanded to include HIV-1 virologically-suppressed adults with estimated creatinine clearance below 15 mL/min on chronic hemodialysis

citations.quote: These data were submitted to support the use of Biktarvy for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in virologically-suppressed, adult patients, with estimated creatinine clearance below 15 mL per minute who are receiving chronic hemodialysis.

description.text: Added safety and efficacy information for use in virologically suppressed, HIV-1 infected patients aged 65 years and over

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides updates to the USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS and CLINICAL STUDIES sections of the United States Prescribing Information (USPI) for Biktarvy, with additional safety and efficacy information pertaining to use of Biktarvy in virologically suppressed, HIV-1 infected subjects aged 65 years and over. Data to support the proposed changes to the Biktarvy USPI were derived from the following clinical trials:

description.text: Expanded to include HIV-1 infected pediatric patients weighing at least 14 kg and added a low-dose tablet

citations.quote: - To expand the patient population for Biktarvy to include HIV-1 infected pediatric patients weighing at least 14 kg. This change is supported by safety and efficacy data in HIV-1 infected, virologically suppressed pediatric subjects, from Cohort 3 of the Clinical Trial GS-US-380-1474.

description.text: Updated Prescribing Information with Week 144 efficacy and safety data for antiretroviral therapy-naïve adults with HIV-1 infection

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides to update the Prescribing Information with additional Week 144 efficacy and safety data for antiretroviral therapy-naïve adult patients with HIV-1 infection. The data include an additional 96 weeks of blinded treatment (Week 144) and 96 weeks of open-label treatment (Week 240) from the original Week 48 approval.

description.text: Added use for treatment of HIV-1 in virologically suppressed adults and pediatric patients on a stable regimen with no known resistance to bictegravir or tenofovir

citations.quote: - New data from trial GS-US-380-4030 to support use of Biktarvy for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in virologically suppressed adults and pediatric patients on a stable HIV-1 treatment regimen with no known resistance to bictegravir or tenofovir

description.text: Added dosing and data supporting use for HIV-1 treatment in pregnant individuals who are virologically suppressed on a stable antiretroviral regimen

citations.quote: - Updates to DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION section with new sub-section 2.4, Recommended Dosage in Pregnant Individuals.

description.text: Expanded to include HIV-1 patients with antiretroviral treatment history who are not virologically suppressed and without known resistance substitutions

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application supports use of Biktarvy in people living with HIV-1 with an antiretroviral treatment history and who are not virologically suppressed, and who have no known or suspected substitutions associated with resistance to the integrase strand inhibitor class, emtricitabine, or tenofovir.

basis.text: Sponsor requested Fast Track Designation on November 10, 2016; on December 9, 2016 FDA denied the request as insufficient information was provided to support an unmet medical need

citations.quote: On December 9, 2016, FDA denied this request as insufficient information was provided to support that B/F/TAF provided for an unmet medical need for the treatment of HIV-1.

basis.text: Priority Review; the NDA was submitted with a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher for priority review consideration

citations.quote: This submission was accompanied with a Tropical Disease Voucher for priority review consideration.
Submission Type; Type of Review	New Molecular Entity; Priority Review

summary.text: BIKTARVY (NDA 210251) was reviewed as a New Molecular Entity under Priority Review, with priority review status obtained via a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher; Fast Track designation was requested but denied. No advisory committee was convened, and the drug received first-cycle approval on standard (not accelerated) approval based on four Phase 3 trials (two Phase 3 trials in treatment-naïve adults, GS-US-380-1489 and GS-US-380-1490, and two Phase 3 trials in virologically-suppressed adults, GS-US-380-1844 and GS-US-380-1878).

citations.quote: Submission Type; Type of Review	New Molecular Entity; Priority Review
This submission was accompanied with a Tropical Disease Voucher for priority review consideration.
On December 9, 2016, FDA denied this request as insufficient information was provided to support that B/F/TAF provided for an unmet medical need for the treatment of HIV-1.

The primary trials that support the safety and efficacy of the B/F/TAF (50/200/25 mg) FDC are two Phase 3 trials in HIV-1 infected, treatment-naïve adults (GS-US-380-1489 and GS-US-380-1490) and two Phase 3 trials in HIV-1 infected, virologically suppressed adults (GS-US-380-1844 and GS-US-380-1878).

requirement.text: Conduct a study in patients 2 years to <18 years old who are HIV-1 infected, virologically suppressed and on a stable antiretroviral regimen, to assess PK, safety, tolerability, and antiviral activity of B/F/TAF as a FDC (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 3322-1 Conduct a study in patients 2 years to <18 years old who are HIV-1 infected, virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) and on a stable antiretroviral regimen at the time of enrollment, to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability, and antiviral activity of bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide as part of a fixed dose combination (FDC) product.

requirement.text: Conduct a study in HIV-1 infected, treatment-naive patients at least 4 weeks and weighing 4 to 12 kg to assess PK, safety, tolerability, and antiviral activity of B/F/TAF, monitored for a minimum of 24 weeks (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 3322-2 Conduct a study in HIV-1 infected, treatment naïve patients at least 4 weeks and weighing 4 to 12 kg to assess the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability, and antiviral activity of bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide. Study participants must be monitored for a minimum of 24 weeks to assess safety and durability of antiviral response.

requirement.text: Conduct a study to evaluate PK and safety of B/F/TAF in neonates (birth to less than 4 weeks of age) who are HIV-1 infected or exposed and at high risk of infection to identify the appropriate dose and establish safety (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 3322-3 Conduct a study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and safety of bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF) in neonates (birth to less than 4 weeks of age) who are HIV-1 infected or exposed and at high risk of infection to identify the appropriate dose and establish the safety of B/F/TAF.
